_comment: SYNTHETIC — hand-built from the documented response shapes in Yahoo's official
Fantasy Sports API guide and from published wrapper-library samples (yfpy,
yahoo_fantasy_api). NOT a live capture. Yahoo API access is gated behind an
approval application and NO live call has ever been made from this repo.
Replace with a real redacted capture once API access is approved.
AUTHORED 2026-08-11 (not captured on any date).
MODELS: GET /fantasy/v2/league/449.l.529351/teams/roster;week=5?format=json
(the batched form — ALL teams' rosters for one week in ONE request;
per-team fetching would be 12x the requests for identical data
against a per-client_id rate limit)
REDACTION: all identifiers invented — team keys, team names and manager
GUIDs (FAKEGUID...) are fake. Player names are real NFL players with
PLAUSIBLE BUT UNVERIFIED numeric ids. No token, email or real GUID appears
anywhere in this directory.
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED — TWO CLAIMS, BOTH NEGATIVE, BOTH EASY TO DISBELIEVE:
1. A ROSTER RESPONSE CARRIES NO POINTS. Search this file: there is no
player_points and no player_stats anywhere in it. Every player ends at
selected_position. Weekly points require the CHAINED form, which is a
separate request — see yahoo_roster_week_with_stats.json. Anyone who
assumes the roster call is enough silently gets NULL points for an
entire backfill.
2. YAHOO HAS NO is_started FIELD. There is no starter flag here either.
Starter status is DERIVED: 'this player's selected_position is not a
bench-like slot IN THIS LEAGUE'. The slot vocabulary comes from the
league's own roster_positions (yahoo_league_settings_snake.json declares
BN and IR for this exact league), which is why parse_rosters() takes
starting/bench/injury slot sets as arguments and leaves is_starter NULL
when they are not supplied. An unknown lineup requirement must produce
an unknown starter flag, never a wrong one — and 'BN' is not a safe
global constant: leagues define IR, IR+, IR-R and NA too.
SHAPE HAZARDS DELIBERATELY PRESENT:
1. ⚠️ THE NUMERIC SUB-RESOURCE WRAPPER. 'roster' is an OBJECT whose scalar
children (coverage_type, week, is_editable) sit at the top level while
its players COLLECTION is nested one level down under the key "0":
"roster": {"coverage_type":"week", "week":"5", "is_editable":0,
This is the shape published wrappers index into — yfpy's data key list
for a team roster is literally ["team","roster","0","players"]. It is
reproduced here because it is the hazard most likely to break the
pipeline: flatten_resource() merges the members of an ARRAY resource but
does not descend into the numeric-key members of an OBJECT one, so
get(roster, "players") returns MISSING and the parse yields ZERO rows
WITHOUT RAISING. See the note at the bottom of this comment.
2. 'team' is an ARRAY whose element 0 is itself an ARRAY of single-key
dicts (one per metadata field) and whose element 1 is the roster
sub-resource. Positional indexing dies here.
3. selected_position is an ARRAY of single-key dicts:
[{coverage_type},{week},{position},{is_flex}] — is_flex is present only
on the W/R/T slot.
4. The two bench-like slots differ: 'BN' and 'IR'. Both must classify as
is_starting_slot=0, and IR must additionally set is_injury_slot=1.
5. eligible_positions is a numeric-key COLLECTION for multi-eligible
players and a BARE OBJECT for the single-eligibility kicker — the
single-element collapse, in the wild, in the middle of a roster.
6. is_editable is 0 (a past week) as a bare INT while week is the STRING
"5" in the same object.
7. One player carries an injury status ('Q') and one carries 'IR' with a
status_full and injury_note. Status is absent, not empty, on healthy
players.
TRUNCATED: 2 teams of the league's 12, and 9 of each team's 16 roster slots
(the league runs QB/RB/RB/WR/WR/TE/W-R-T/K/DEF + 6 BN + 1 IR). Reason: the
remaining teams and bench spots are byte-identical code paths; what is kept
is one of every DISTINCT slot kind — a starter, a flex, a bench and an IR —
which is the whole of what the derivation depends on.
⚠️ KNOWN DISAGREEMENT WITH THE SHIPPED PARSER, 2026-08-11. Against parse.py
at PARSER_VERSION 1.0.0 this file parses to 0 roster snapshots and 0 players,
SILENTLY — no exception — because flatten_resource() merges the members of an
ARRAY resource but does not descend into the numeric-key members of an OBJECT
one, so get(roster, "players") is MISSING. That was reported to the parser
author rather than papered over: removing the "0" wrapper would make the
fixture green and leave the pipeline wrong against the real API.
EXPECTED ONCE THE PARSER HANDLES THE WRAPPER (measured by hoisting roster
["0"] in a harness, with parse.py untouched):
fantasy_roster_snapshots  18      fantasy_players  18
is_starter=1  14   is_bench=1  2   is_injury_slot=1  2
the two W/R/T rows carry is_flex_slot=1
Those are the numbers to assert. If a live capture ever proves Yahoo does
NOT wrap here, delete the "0": { } level in both teams and this note with it.
